exemplars.title: StorySage: Conversational Autobiography Writing Powered by a Multi-Agent Framework
exemplars.why: StorySage is the strongest structural match because it explicitly defines its depicted interaction flow as one session, indicating that autobiographical conversation is organized as a bounded episode rather than an always-open thread. The available excerpt does not establish the session’s entry condition, terminal state, or cross-session reference rules, so the exemplar is strong but incompletely evidenced.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: StorySage ranks above Poet-Weaver because its evidence explicitly says the flow defines a single session, whereas Poet-Weaver’s caption merely labels a flow as being for a reflection session.

exemplars.title: Poet-Weaver: Reflecting on Communication Failure in Personal Relationships With Stylized AI-Generated Conversation Digests
exemplars.why: Poet-Weaver packages sensitive conversation reflection into a named session with its own interaction flow, plausibly turning reflection into a discrete episode. However, the caption alone does not verify a system-imposed close, repeated-session reset, or limits on what subsequent sessions may reference.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Poet-Weaver ranks above HINT because it associates session-bounding with the user-facing interaction flow, while HINT’s successive sessions may only be rounds in a longitudinal testing protocol.

exemplars.title: HINT: Integration Testing for AI-based features with Humans in the Loop
exemplars.why: HINT deliberately divides an evolving AI experience across successive sessions, making repeated episodes part of how the experience is tested. It is only a weak exemplar: the quote does not demonstrate defined openings and closes, a fixed within-session flow, or session-scoped context, and the sessions may belong to the evaluation protocol rather than the interface itself.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: HINT ranks above StayFocused because successive sessions are explicitly used to structure an evolving AI experience, whereas StayFocused describes user-set non-screen intervals and therefore conflicts with the pattern’s requirement that the system impose the interaction boundary.

notes: I retained the consensus ordering and excluded StayFocused. Its evidence describes sessions set by users, which directly conflicts with the definition’s system-imposed boundary and resembles a focus timer more than a bounded interaction flow. I reduced Poet-Weaver from 2.43 to 2.25 and HINT from 1.83 to 1.55 because neither excerpt confirms the required terminal state or session-scoped reference behavior; neither adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should treat Poet-Weaver and especially HINT as provisional exemplars: their evidence names sessions but does not expose the complete structural signature. StorySage is the only selection whose excerpt directly says that a flow defines one session, though even it lacks evidence for opening, closure, repetition, and cross-session scoping.
